body:
Currently the requirements about TLS say "Verify that **only the latest recommended** […]":

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **12.1.1** | Verify that **only the latest recommended versions** of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The latest version of the TLS protocol must be the preferred option. | 1 | v5.0.be-9.4.2 |
| **12.1.2** | Verify that **only the latest recommended cipher suites** are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy. | 2 | v5.0.be-9.4.1 |

Should we say: "only approved instead" and include a list of approved TLS versions in the appendix?

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **12.1.1** | Verify that **only approved** versions of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The latest version of the TLS protocol must be the preferred option. | 1 | v5.0.be-9.4.2 |
| **12.1.2** | Verify that only cipher suites using approved cryptographic mechanisms are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy. | 2 | v5.0.be-9.4.1 |

comments.body: This seems like a very reasonable change, +1

Do we need this in the appendix or can we rely on the cheat sheet and provide a reference:
https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Transport_Layer_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
That is the first in our references list for that chapter but we could be more explicit in section text
I'm a bit confused at your comments, Josh. This is a small change suggestion to two requirements (12.1.1 and 12.1.2), not the reference list or appendix.

@randomstuff said:

> Should we say: "only approved instead" and include a list of approved TLS versions in the appendix?

My response was basically:

> Do we need this in the appendix or can we rely on the cheat sheet and provide a reference:
https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Transport_Layer_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
>That (the cheatsheet) is the first in our references list for that chapter but we could be more explicit in section text

I think including ciphers in the appendix would be duplication of the cheatsheet or if we think something is missing in the cheat sheet then we should maybe update the cheatsheet.

Also, @jmanico do we think the cheatsheet could be considered to have "approved options" or do you think it is more accurately classified as "recommended options"

> Also, @jmanico do we think the cheatsheet could be considered to have "approved options" or do you think it is more accurately classified as "recommended options

We suggest in the cheat sheet:

_General purpose web applications should default to TLS 1.3 (support TLS 1.2 if necessary) with all other protocols disabled_

And there are very few cipher options for TLS 1.3. So if you take that advice and only enable TLS 1.3 it's close to "approved".

But I could kindly as @randomstuff and others to take a look at the CS and give it a once over before the upcoming ASVS 5 release.

I am comfortable making the cheat sheet suggestions more aggressive than they are now.

> I think including ciphers in the appendix would be duplication of the cheatsheet

We currently do have list of approved *ciphers*. I do not suggest having a list of approved *ciphersuites*. We can use what we already have in the appendix: a list of approved ciphers, AEAD, hash functions.

Moreover, I would intent the list of approved cryptographic mechanisms in the appendix is to be a default baseline which is intended be customized or modified by the organization using the ASVS eg. when new cryptographic mechanisms become mainstream, or deprecated, or for aligning with some regulation which overrides it. In other words "approved" should be understood as understood in the scope of the project and not necessarily approved by the ASVS appendix.

I think "latest recommended" was relatively understandable. I think you would need to clarify in the requirement what "approved" means, ideally without us needing to create new documentation requirement.
I am honestly ok with either way but after all the work @randomstuff has done for this standard I want to sure his concerns are addressed. Any other thoughts on this @randomstuff ?

The "approved" wording would make these could closer to the other requirements (eg. in V11).

And I find "latest recommended cipher suites" somewhat ambiguous in its interpretation when reading fast ("latest cipher suites which are recommended"? "Latest reommendation of ciphersuites"? "Latest ciphersuites"?). But in all honesty, we can understand the meaning of the current formulation. Maybe it's all right.

As for "12.1.1", I think it would be nice to list approved TLS versions in the appendix. That would align with other approved crypto things in the appendix.

To be clear it is working OK as it is but I find if better (more consistent) the with the approved wording.

@danielcuthbert, @unprovable any feedback on that?

@randomstuff, so to me saying "recommended" allows us to clearly point towards the TLS cheat sheet or our appendix. Specifically, I think saying "only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol" makes a lot of sense as TLS versions are kinda chronological in that the latest versions 1.2 and 1.3 are what are currently recommended. On the other hand, I guess saying "only the latest recommended cipher suites" does not make quite as much sense and would be better as "only recommended cipher suites".

Saying "approved" makes me question whether we are talking about approved by the company developing the application, approved by NIST, etc? To me it seems a little clearer.

So my current proposal for V12 would be to leave 12.1.1 as it is and modify 12.1.2 to be:

"_Verify that only ~~the latest~~ recommended cipher suites are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy._"

I am very open to alternative suggestions but if we want to use the term "approved" it would need to be clarified.

For ciphersuites in the appendix, I would request that you open a separate issue which references this one.

@randomstuff just to add to this, I am happy with the use of approved in V11 because there we specifically provide approved ciphers in the appendix and in #3018 I explain this.

For V12, we don't have the information in the appendix so I stand by what I said in the previous comment https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2992#issuecomment-2817724173

> [@randomstuff](https://github.com/randomstuff) just to add to this, I am happy with the use of approved in V11 because there we specifically provide approved ciphers in the appendix and in [#3018](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/3018) I explain this.
> 
> For V12, we don't have the information in the appendix so I stand by what I said in the previous comment [#2992 (comment)](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2992#issuecomment-2817724173)

This make a lot more sense, thanks Josh.
Based on @randomstuff's thumbs up [to my proposal](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2992#issuecomment-2817724173), I have opened #3032

title: Clarify requirement about "latest recommended" TLS versions and ciphersuites
